Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Emma Lopez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover seven key aspects: performance by key categories and brands; organic sales growth guidance for next quarter and the year; decomposition of organic sales growth into volume, price, and mix; supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings impact; price elasticity observations; organic sales growth rate; and gross margin guidance and key assumptions.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.4 billion, representing a 7.2% increase compared to the prior year, or 5.2% on an organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by productivity gains, favorable mix, and disciplined pricing. Operating income was $620 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.52. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me now dive into our performance by key categories and brands, which continues to underscore the resilience and strategic focus of our portfolio here at GCB. As you know, our business is anchored in four core pillars—Snacks, Beverages, Personal Care, and Household Essentials—spanning over 50 leading brands with a combined global market share of approximately 8% in our addressable categories. In Q3 FY2024, these segments delivered aggregate net sales growth of 7.2% year-over-year, or 5.8% on an organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. This was fueled by a mix of volume gains in high-margin power brands, targeted pricing actions averaging 4-6% across the portfolio to offset raw material inflation, and distribution expansion into 1.2 points of ACV globally.

Starting with Snacks, our brightest star, which grew net sales 12.4% year-over-year, or 10.9% organically—well ahead of the category's global IRI-tracked growth of 4.2%. Volumes were up 3.8%, with velocity improving 2.1 points, driven by our relentless focus on innovation and shopper fundamentals. CrunchMax, our flagship savory brand akin to a Lay's or Doritos powerhouse, surged 15% in sales, capturing 1.1 share points in North American retail channels through our MaxFlavor line extension—think bold, limited-time flavors like Truffle BBQ and Spicy Sriracha Lime, which posted triple-digit distribution gains in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club.

SweetBites cookies rounded out the category winners, up 11% with strong e-comm penetration; we're now at 25% digital sales mix here, versus the category average of 15%, thanks to targeted Shopify partnerships and Amazon velocity programs. Challenges? We saw some softness in emerging markets due to palm oil cost spikes—up 22% YoY—but our forward hedging program locked in 85% of next year's needs at favorable rates.

Regionally, North America led with 14% growth, bolstered by in-store shelving resets yielding 0.8 ACV points. EMEA was solid at 9%, despite UK volume pressures from health halo shifts, where we're countering with air-fried, lower-sodium variants. APAC exploded 18%, riding China's snackification trend—CrunchMax volumes there doubled via Tmall and JD.com exclusives. Strategically, we're doubling down on premium pricing architecture: 60% of Snack SKUs now carry a 20%+ price premium over private label, delivering 450 bps of margin expansion YTD.

Shifting to Beverages, net sales were flat year-over-year at +0.2%, or -1.5% organically, reflecting ongoing consumer trade-downs in sugary carbonated soft drinks amid GLP-1 medication impacts and wellness trends—global CSD volumes per Nielsen are down 2-3%. That said, we're seeing green shoots: Q3 marked our first YoY volume growth in six quarters at +0.5%, thanks to non-carb diversification.

Zest Cola, our century-old icon competing with Coke and Pepsi, held steady with -1% sales but gained 0.3 share points in USD markets through Zest Zero Sugar reformulations—now 40% of the portfolio, with stevia-sweetened variants up 25%. VitaBoost energy drinks were the category MVP, exploding 22% on the back of functional claims like focus + immunity, mirroring Red Bull's playbook but at a more accessible price point. New Product Innovation here included RTD protein shakes, which hit 15% repeat purchase rates in test markets.

Regionally, LATAM shone with 8% growth, defying Argentina's hyperinflation via local sourcing of cane sugar, down 10% cost vs. imports. North America faced -3% pressure from soda taxes in states like Colorado, but we're mitigating with 500 bps of pricing elasticity testing. EMEA volumes dipped 2% on EU sugar reduction mandates, prompting our SweetSwap initiative—swapping HFCS for fruit juices in 70% of recipes. Looking ahead, we're investing $150 million in a new aseptic filling line in Mexico to chase the $20 billion RTD functional beverage TAM, targeting 15% category growth by FY2025.

Personal Care delivered a stellar 9.1% net sales increase, or 7.6% organic, outpacing the category's 3.5% global growth per Euromonitor. This reflects our beauty from within positioning, blending indulgence with efficacy amid rising at-home pampering post-pandemic.

SilkFlow shampoos led with 12% growth, gaining 1.2 share points in prestige mass channels like Ulta and Walmart beauty aisles, driven by our sulfate-free, microbiome-friendly SilkBiome launch—now 30% of sales, with 2x trial-to-repeat conversion versus legacy SKUs. FreshGuard deodorants climbed 10%, capitalizing on aluminum-free trends akin to Native's rise, with eucalyptus-infused variants boosting Amazon rankings to top-5 in category.

Regionally, APAC was phenomenal at 14% growth, fueled by India's premiumization wave—SilkFlow volumes up 25% via Flipkart exclusives and D2C subscriptions. North America hit 8%, with clean beauty claims resonating in Gen Z; we're at 22% sustainable packaging penetration here. EMEA grew 6%, tempered by Germany's plastic taxes, but our refill pod program for FreshGuard reduced virgin plastic by 40% and lifted loyalty metrics 15%. Margins expanded 200 bps on formula optimization—sourcing bio-based surfactants cut costs 8%. Strategically, we're pruning underperformers: divested two regional soap brands for $80 million, reallocating to high-ROIC NPI like CBD-infused conditioners targeting the $5 billion global wellness hair care segment.

Rounding out with Household Essentials, up 6.3% net sales or 4.9% organic—inline with category averages but with superior margins. Volumes grew 1.2%, a reversal from last year's declines, as consumers prioritized performance over price in a high-inflation environment.

CleanWave laundry detergent rose 8%, stealing 0.7 share points from Tide and Persil via concentrated pods—now 55% of volume, delivering 25% less packaging waste and appealing to eco-shoppers. AbsorbPro paper towels gained 5%, with quilted UltraGrip sheets winning in club stores on absorbency claims validated by SGS lab tests.

North America drove 7% growth, with velocity up 1.5 points from P&G-like bundling promos. LATAM surged 10% despite Brazil's currency woes, thanks to localized enzyme formulations slashing water usage 20%. EMEA was flat on energy surcharges for pulp, but our switch to FSC-certified bamboo fibers in AbsorbPro cut costs 12% long-term. APAC grew 9%, riding Vietnam's urbanization boom.

Inflation bit here—wood pulp up 15% YoY—but our value engineering team reformulated 40% of SKUs, yielding 300 bps gross margin lift. Forward, we're launching CleanWave EcoDose dispensers in 2024, aiming for subscription revenue streams à la Method's model, targeting 10% digital mix.

Across categories, power brands—those with >$500 million sales and 10%+ growth—now represent 65% of our portfolio, up from 55% last year, delivering 9% organic growth versus 2% for the rest. This reflects our Focus 15 strategy: concentrating 80% of innovation spend on 15 hero brands. Distributionally, we're at 92% ACV in North America, with 2 points gained via Kroger and Albertsons resets. Sustainability is table stakes—75% of products now verified carbon-neutral per lifecycle assessments, resonating in Nielsen sustainability surveys where we're +5 points above category averages.

Challenges persist: FX headwinds shaved 120 bps off top-line, and U.S. private label aggression pressured mix by 50 bps. But our pricing discipline—elasticity at -2.5x versus historical -3.5x—and supply chain resiliency, inventory turns at 8.2x, position us well.

Now, let's break down the decomposition of our organic sales growth of 5.2% for the quarter, ahead of our guided range of 4-5%, and up 80 basis points year-over-year. This performance underscores the resilience of our portfolio amid a still-challenging macroeconomic environment, characterized by moderating inflation—down to 2.8% globally from 4.1% a year ago—and softening consumer demand in certain value segments.

To break it down, our organic growth was driven by a balanced volume contribution of +2.1%, pricing of +2.5%, and favorable mix of +0.6%. Starting with volume: +2.1%. This marks our strongest volume quarter in five periods, reflecting successful execution of our Volume Momentum 2025 initiative—a multi-year program investing $450 million in shopper marketing, in-store activations, and velocity-building trade promotions. We saw broad-based gains across categories, led by our Health & Wellness segment, which grew volumes 4.2% on the back of innovations like our new plant-based protein bars under the VitalFuel brand, which ramped to 15% household penetration in North America within three months of launch—mirroring the explosive growth we saw with Kellogg's RXBAR acquisition playbook.

Regionally: North America, 55% of sales, volumes up 2.8%, fueled by distribution gains in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club, where we expanded facings for our NovaPure household cleaners by 12%. However, we lapped some pandemic-era pantry-loading, tempering growth versus last year. EMEA, 20% of sales, +1.9%, with standout performance in the UK and Germany from our Everyday Essentials refresh—low-cal snack packs that captured share from private labels amid 3% category contraction. LATAM, 15% of sales, +3.4%, our growth engine, driven by Brazil's informal channel expansion, where we deployed micro-depot logistics to boost availability to 92%—up from 85%. APAC, 10% of sales, flat at +0.1%, pressured by China's zero-COVID hangover and competition from local players like Uni-President in beverages, but we're gaining traction with premium hydration products in India.

Challenges persist in mass-market beverages, down 1.2% on volume due to health-conscious downtrading, but offset by our RTD coffee line, NovaBrew, which grew 18% on e-commerce velocity.

Pricing: +2.5%. Pricing remains a key profitability lever as input costs stabilize—our CPI basket for commodities like cocoa, palm oil, and PET resin fell 5% sequentially. We took disciplined, list-price actions averaging 3.2% across the portfolio, below the 4.5% we implemented last year, focusing on elasticity-tested SKUs. This reflects our Smart Price Architecture framework, which segments pricing by channel and consumer occasion to minimize volume elasticity—running at -1.8x overall, better than the industry's -2.2x benchmark per Nielsen data.

Segment highlights: Snacks & Confectionery, 30% of sales, +3.1% pricing, capturing 150 bps of margin expansion despite cocoa inflation lingering at +25% YoY. Premium chocolate lines like our LuxeTruffle range justified 5-7% increases via superior storytelling around ethical sourcing. Beverages, 25% of sales, +2.8%, with functional waters and energy drinks leading; we held the line on carbonated soft drinks to defend share against PepsiCo's pricing aggression. Household & Personal Care, 45% of sales, +2.2%, where everyday items like laundry pods saw modest hikes, balanced by value packs to retain price-sensitive households.

Regionally, LATAM pricing was highest at +4.1% to offset currency devaluations, while North America moderated to +1.9% amid FTC scrutiny on grocery concentration.

Mix: +0.6%. Favorable mix continues to benefit from our premiumization strategy, shifting 2.5 points of portfolio revenue toward higher-margin power brands—now 68% of sales, up from 62% three years ago. This is driven by Portfolio Elevation 2.0, which reallocates 20% of our $2.8 billion innovation budget to super-premium and health-adjacent SKUs, akin to Unilever's shift with Dove or P&G's SK-II playbook.

Key shifts: Health & Wellness up 420 bps in mix, led by organic baby foods and keto-friendly snacks, growing 12% vs. total snacks at 4%. Premium household cleaners, e.g., enzyme-based NovaEco line, gained 180 bps, resonating with sustainability trends—our eco-portfolio now 25% of category sales, per IRI scan data. Drag from legacy mass beverages, down 150 bps, as consumers trade up to low-sugar alternatives.

Regionally, APAC mix improved +1.2% on premium beauty masks in Southeast Asia, while EMEA saw headwinds from discounter dominance.

This decomposition validates our three-pillar growth algorithm: innovate relentlessly, with 12 new billion-dollar brands in pipeline; win at the point of sale, omnichannel distribution to 95% ACV; and price for value, targeting 50 bps annual mix tailwind. Amid category growth of just 2.1% globally—per Euromonitor—our outperformance stems from leading in megatrends like wellness, 22% of portfolio, and sustainability, certified packaging on 75% of products.

Our organic sales growth of 5.2% came in ahead of our guidance range of 3% to 4% and marked our eighth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth. This builds on the 4.8% we posted in Q2 and compares favorably to the 2.1% industry average reported by NielsenIQ for the broader CPG sector during the same period. Breaking it down, pricing contributed 3.4%, reflecting disciplined execution amid persistent input cost inflation—think cocoa prices up 25% year-over-year and palm oil volatility—while volume/mix added a solid 1.8%, driven by share gains in key categories.

By segment, in Beauty & Personal Care, 35% of total sales, organic growth accelerated to 8.1%, fueled by premiumization trends. Our flagship anti-aging skincare line, RenewVital, saw double-digit volume growth of 12%, gaining 110 basis points of market share in North America per IRI data, outpacing competitors like L'Oréal and Estée Lauder. We leaned into e-commerce here, with DTC sales up 25% thanks to our AI-powered personalization engine, which recommends products based on skin analytics from our app—now with over 5 million active users.

Home Care delivered 4.3% organic growth, benefiting from our sustainability initiatives. The launch of our EcoShield laundry pods—plant-based, recyclable packaging—captured 8% market share in Europe within three months, helping us offset private label pressure. Pricing here was up 4.2%, but volumes held steady at +0.1%, as consumers traded down less than expected amid cooling inflation.

Our Food & Beverage segment was flat at 0.2% organic growth, weighed down by softer snack volumes in APAC due to post-COVID normalization. However, our nutrition bars under the VitalFuel brand grew 15%, riding the high-protein wave similar to what KIND and RXBAR have seen, with expanded distribution into 2,000 additional Walmart and Kroger doors.

Regionally, North America, our largest market at 45% of sales, grew 4.5% organically, with volume up 1.2% as we gained 60 basis points overall versus the category averages—strong in grocery but softer in mass channels amid Amazon's aggressive private label push. EMEA was the standout at 6.1%, propelled by pricing discipline in the UK and Germany, where we passed through 70% of cost inflation without losing share, per Kantar data. Latin America surged 7.2%, thanks to volume recovery in Brazil's hygiene category post-flooding disruptions and our new sachet packaging for low-income consumers, mirroring Unilever's successful strategies there. Asia-Pacific dipped -1.3%, primarily from China lockdowns impacting out-of-home foodservice, but we're mitigating with localized innovations like low-sugar ready-to-drink teas tailored to Gen Z preferences.

Behind these numbers are several technical initiatives that have been game-changers. Our supply chain resilience program, Project Horizon, which we've invested $250 million in over the past 18 months, reduced stockouts by 40% globally through AI-forecasting and nearshoring—critical in a world of Red Sea disruptions. Precision pricing analytics: using machine learning models trained on 10 years of IRI and Nielsen POS data, we've optimized everyday low pricing versus high-low promotions, boosting margins by 120 basis points without sacrificing volumes. R&D spend up 15% to $450 million annually has yielded 22 new product launches this year, with a 75% success rate in trial-to-repeat purchase, well above the industry norm of 50%.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on share gain through superior innovation and execution. We've outpaced the total CPG market by 300 basis points YTD, per Circana, by doubling down on health & wellness—now 28% of our portfolio—and sustainability credentials that resonate with millennials. Challenges remain, like tariff risks in LATAM and softening consumer sentiment in the US, where 62% of households are still inflation-weary per our proprietary surveys. But our forward coverage is strong, with 85% of Q4 pricing locked in.

Looking ahead, before I hand it back, let me provide more color on our organic sales growth guidance for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2025. Organic sales growth excludes the impacts of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange, allowing us to focus purely on the underlying health of our core business—volume, pricing, and mix dynamics across our portfolio of household staples, beauty, personal care, and nutrition brands.

For Q4, we are guiding to organic sales growth of 4% to 6%. This reflects a sequential moderation from our Q3 print of 5.2%, but still a solid outperformance versus the CPG industry consensus of low-single digits, as tracked by NielsenIQ and IRI data. Looking out to full FY 2025, we expect organic growth of 5% to 7%, positioning us at the high end of peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever, who have guided mid-single digits amid persistent consumer value-seeking behaviors.

Pricing and mix: stabilizing tailwinds, 2-3 points of growth. Pricing actions, which contributed 4.1 points in Q3, are expected to moderate to 1.5-2 points in Q4 and 2-2.5 points for FY '25 as inflation eases—U.S. CPI for food and beverages is now trending at 1.2% year-over-year, per BLS data. We've locked in forward contracts for 80% of our key inputs like palm oil, PET resin, and cocoa, mitigating volatility seen earlier this year with cocoa prices spiking 40% on West African supply constraints. Mix remains a bright spot at 0.5-1 point, driven by premiumization in high-margin segments. For instance, our FreshGlow Ultra-Concentrate laundry pods—up 15% in velocity—are pulling through 2x the gross margin of our legacy powders, echoing P&G's Tide Pods success.

Volume: recovery momentum, 2-4 points. Volume growth accelerates to 2-3% in Q4 from 1.8% in Q3, fueled by distribution gains and innovation. We're targeting 200 basis points of shelf space expansion in North American grocery, per Circana analytics, particularly in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club where private label pressures are easing. Health and wellness trends are key here—our NutriVital protein snack bars, reformulated with plant-based pea protein to tap the 12% CAGR in that subcategory per Euromonitor, posted 18% household penetration growth in Q3.

Regionally: North America, 55% of sales, guiding 5-7% organic growth. Our largest market sees the strongest performance, with volume up 3% on e-commerce acceleration—Amazon and Walmart+ now represent 22% of U.S. sales, up from 18% last year. Premium beauty lines like GlowEssence serums are gaining share in Ulta and Sephora, countering Coty's slowdown in mass prestige. Headwinds from tariff uncertainties on Mexican imports are minimal, as 70% of our supply chain is North America-sourced.

EMEA, 25% of sales, 3-5% growth: Moderating from Q3's 6% due to soft UK volumes amid cost-of-living pressures—Nielsen reports a 1% category decline there. Offset by double-digit growth in our PureSpring hydration beverages in Germany and France, where we're launching recyclable aluminum cans ahead of EU single-use plastic bans. Market share up 50 bps vs. Danone in still water.

APAC, 15% of sales, 6-8% growth: The growth engine, led by India and China. In India, sachet packs of our SpiceEssence seasonings drove 25% volume in modern trade via Reliance Retail, tapping rural recovery post-monsoon. China beauty e-commerce via Tmall is +30% YoY, though we're monitoring deflationary pricing from local players like Pechoin.

Latin America, 5% of sales, 4-6% growth: Brazil home care volumes rebounding 5% on affordability packs, but Argentina hyperinflation caps pricing at 50% local CPI—FX-neutralized via our 90% local-for-local sourcing.

This outlook is anchored in three pillars: innovation, 20% of '25 sales target; route-to-market optimization; and sustainability-led productivity. We're rolling out 15 SKUs in Q4, including low-sodium reformulations for NutriVital to capture the 8% U.S. better-for-you snack growth per SPINS data. Tech investments like AI-driven demand sensing—partnered with Blue Yonder—have reduced stockouts by 30%, boosting service levels to 97%. On sustainability, our Planet Positive program, with 100% recyclable packaging by '27, has unlocked 1 point of premium pricing in Europe and retailer partnerships like Tesco's Closed Loop initiative.

Risks to note: elevated input costs if El Niño disrupts 2025 ag yields, or a deeper U.S. consumer slowdown—our IRI shopper panels show 15% trading down to private label in staples. But with $450 million in FY '25 productivity savings, COGS and A&P optimization, we're flexing 50 bps of gross margin expansion to fund trials and promotions.

In summary, our 5-7% FY '25 organic guidance reflects disciplined execution in a normalizing macro, with volume resurgence and premium mix outpacing the industry. We're well-positioned to deliver another year of top-quartile growth.

Turning to gross margins, in Q3 we delivered 48.2%, up 70 basis points year-over-year and 40 basis points sequentially. This reflects the continued payoff from our Supply Chain Excellence Program, which generated $185 million in productivity savings—about 160 basis points of gross margin accretion—through advanced manufacturing automation and AI-optimized procurement. We also benefited from favorable product mix, with premium segments like our organic snack lines, Vitality Organics bars up 12% YoY, and plant-based beverages outpacing value tiers by 300 bps. Pricing discipline held firm at +2.8%, countering softer consumer demand amid persistent inflation.

Looking ahead, we're raising our FY24 gross margin guidance to 48.5% to 49.0%, from our prior 48.0% to 48.5% range. For Q4, we expect 49.2%, implying roughly 100 bps of sequential expansion. Peering into FY25, we're guiding to 49.5% to 50.0%, positioning us toward our long-term target of 51%+ by FY27 as we lap easier comps and scale structural initiatives.

Key assumptions: Pricing and Revenue Growth Management, +120 bps tailwind. We're assuming +2.5% to +3.0% net pricing across FY25, flat to up slightly from FY24. This embeds disciplined everyday pricing in North America, where we'll take modest increases on high-velocity SKUs like our Vitality Energy drinks, competing with Red Bull and Monster, to offset private label pressure from Walmart's Great Value and Costco's Kirkland lines.

In Europe, pricing softens to +1.5% due to regulatory scrutiny and retailer pushback, e.g., Tesco and Carrefour demanding lower list prices, but premiumization in beauty, our anti-aging serums akin to Dove or L'Oréal, supports +4% mix benefits. Emerging Markets see +5% pricing, led by Brazil and India, where inflation-linked contracts with local retailers like Reliance Retail provide natural hedges. RGM investments, including AI-powered dynamic pricing tools similar to those piloted by Procter & Gamble, will optimize trade spend efficiency, limiting promotional erosion to under 50 bps.

Commodity costs and sourcing: neutral to +20 bps headwind. Input cost inflation moderates to 1-2% YoY in FY25, down from 4% in FY24. Cocoa prices, spiked 25% YTD due to West African crop failures—Ivory Coast and Ghana supply ~70% globally—are largely hedged through FY25 at +10%—mitigated by forward contracts covering 80% of needs and strategic shifts to almond and oat alternatives in our chocolate-coated snacks.

Palm oil volatility, up 8% on Indonesian export curbs, impacts Household segment margins but is offset by RSPO-certified sustainable sourcing, which unlocked $25 million in premium supplier rebates. PET resin and aluminum for beverages remain pressured +3% from energy costs, but our circular economy initiatives—recycling 40% of PET via partnerships like those with Coca-Cola's World Without Waste—yielded 30 bps savings in Q3. Overall, we assume a 60/40 hedge coverage on key ags, wheat, sugar, soy, with FX translating neutral.

Volume and mix: +80 bps tailwind. Organic volume growth of 1.0-1.5% assumes stabilization in downtrading trends. In North America, consumers trading down to private labels, 15% share gain for Aldi's snacks, caps Food & Beverage volumes at +0.5%, but premium health platforms grow +8%. Europe volumes flat as inflation-weary shoppers favor discounters, Lidl, Aldi, offset by +3% mix from eco-friendly Household products, concentrated laundry pods like Persil Discs. EM volumes +3-4%, fueled by middle-class expansion in Asia-Pacific, Indonesia's e-commerce boom via Shopee. Mix shifts to higher-margin innovations: 20% of FY25 launches are super-premium, collagen-infused yogurts rivaling Chobani, targeting 55%+ category margins.

Productivity and supply chain: +150 bps tailwind. SCEP ramps to $750 million in FY25 savings, +15% YoY, or 220 bps gross margin expansion pre-inflation. Breakdown: 40% from factory digitization, IoT sensors reducing downtime 25%, akin to PepsiCo's smart plants; 30% procurement, zero-based sourcing cut indirects 12%; 20% logistics, DC network optimization post-Port of LA disruptions, targeting 5% freight savings; 10% overhead, GenAI for demand forecasting, slashing obsolescence 18%. We're on track for 95% OTIF delivery, up from 88% in FY22, enhancing resilience against Red Sea disruptions, which added 2% to ocean freight in Q3.

Foreign exchange and other: -10 bps headwind. USD at 105-108 vs. basket assumes modest drag from EM currencies, BRL, INR weakening 3-5%. We hedge 70% of exposures. Tariff risks minimal, <5% China sourcing; steel duties on cans passed through via clauses.

Risks and sensitivities: a 1% swing in commodity inflation impacts FY25 margins by 25 bps; 1% pricing miss costs 40 bps; FX 5% stronger USD hurts 15 bps. Upside from faster premium adoption or SCEP over-delivery could push us to 50.5%.

Strategically, this guidance underscores our Margin First, Growth Second playbook—echoing Unilever's productivity-led recovery—prioritizing structural fixes over short-term volume chases. We're investing $1.2 billion in capex, 3.5% of sales, for next-gen facilities, like our Texas mega-plant for aseptic beverages, ensuring we outpace peers like Colgate-Palmolive, 48% margins, and Kellogg, 42%.

Finally, on price elasticity observations, which have been a key driver of our top-line resilience amid a still-challenging macroeconomic backdrop. Price elasticity measures the sensitivity of consumer demand to price changes—how volume responds to our pricing actions. In CPG, where we operate across snacks, beverages, and household essentials, understanding and optimizing elasticity is table stakes for sustaining margins in an era of persistent inflation, private label aggression, and shifting trade-down behaviors.

Our portfolio-wide price elasticity coefficient improved to -1.05 in Q3, up from -1.18 in Q2 and a more elastic -1.35 this time last year. This means a 1% price increase now yields only a 1.05% volume decline, versus 1.35% a year ago—a clear sign of strengthening brand equity and consumer tolerance for our everyday pricing. This 22% year-over-year improvement in elasticity contributed roughly 150 basis points to our organic revenue growth, helping us deliver 4.2% net price realization despite softer volumes in certain categories.

By segment, in Snacks—our powerhouse with brands like CrunchTime bars and Zestify chips—elasticity tightened to -0.75, reflecting deep loyalty among Gen Z and millennial households. Here, premium innovations like our 15% protein-boosted CrunchTime line have decoupled price from volume; we took a 7% list price hike in July, absorbing only a 5% volume dip, thanks to targeted in-store sampling and TikTok-driven campaigns. This mirrors what we've seen at peers like Mondelez with their Oreo Thins—consumers are trading up within trusted brands rather than fleeing to private labels.

Beverages tell a different story, with elasticity at -1.45, more pronounced due to category promiscuity and functional drink proliferation. Our Sparkle energy waters faced a 1.8% volume hit from a 6% MSP increase in August, exacerbated by competition from Red Bull's zero-sugar variants and PepsiCo's Gatorade push into hydration. However, we're countering this with technical initiatives: we've rolled out AI-powered dynamic pricing pilots with Kroger and Albertsons, using real-time Nielsen scan data and IRI elasticity models to micro-adjust shelf prices by store cluster. Early results? A 12% uplift in promo ROI, shaving elasticity to -1.32 in test banners.

Household Essentials rounded out at -0.95, our most inelastic bucket, buoyed by staple positioning akin to P&G's Tide Pods. Our CleanBurst laundry pods saw just a 0.9% volume drop on a 5.5% price lift, as households prioritize efficacy over cost in this must-have space.

Regionally, North America, which drove 55% of our sales, elasticity held steady at -1.02—resilient despite Walmart's everyday low pricing squeezing our Aisle 1 slots. We offset this with loyalty apps tied to our Everyday Rewards program, mirroring Target Circle's success, which preserved 80% of pass-through pricing.

Europe was softer at -1.22, hit by Aldi/Lidl private label share gains to 32% in fabric care, per Kantar data. Inflation fatigue in the UK and Germany amplified trade-down, but our Euro-specific value tier—CleanBurst Basics at 20% below core—reversed 60% of the elasticity penalty.

Emerging markets shone brightest, with LATAM elasticity at -0.92, down from -1.45 YoY, fueled by aspirational premiumization in Brazil and Mexico. Here, a 9% ASP increase on Sparkle aguas frescas flavors yielded just an 8% volume dip, as middle-class consumers emulate U.S. trends amid peso/dollar volatility. In APAC, Indonesia's halal-certified Zestify variants tightened to -0.85, leveraging Shopee e-comm exclusives to bypass wet market commoditization.

Strategically, these observations are reshaping our playbook. First, we're accelerating digital twins of our pricing engine—leveraging SymphonyAI and our internal ML models trained on 5+ years of ACNielsen POS data—to forecast elasticity at the SKU-store-week level, targeting a further 15% tightening by FY24. Second, we're doubling down on non-price levers: R&D investment in high-efficacy formulas, e.g., 30% more concentrated CleanBurst pods, to justify premiums, much like Unilever's Persil advancements. Third, promotion discipline is key—we've cut depth on Snacks by 200 bps to -18% of revenue, focusing on frequency over discount, which preserved gross margins at 48.2%.

Looking ahead, we expect elasticity to hold in the -1.05 to -1.10 range for Q4, assuming CPI moderates to 3%. Risks include deeper private label penetration if retailers like Costco expand Kirkland CPG lines, but our brand moat—bolstered by $250 million in 2023 media spend—positions us well. This elasticity edge is why we're confident in our full-year guidance: 3-5% organic growth and 100 bps of margin expansion.

After me, Raj will discuss our supply chain initiatives.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management. Diving deeper into one of the key drivers behind our strong margin performance this quarter: our supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings. In the CPG space, where we're battling persistent commodity inflation—think cocoa prices up 40% YoY amid West African supply disruptions and palm oil volatility tied to El Niño effects—these initiatives are mission-critical for protecting gross margins and funding growth investments.

Our supply chain productivity program delivered $285 million in run-rate savings year-to-date, a 12% acceleration from the $250 million we realized in FY23. This contributed 170 basis points of gross margin expansion in the quarter, helping us offset 250 bps of input cost inflation across our Snacks, Beverages, and Household Essentials segments. On a two-year stacked basis, we've now captured over $750 million in cumulative savings since launching our Supply Chain 2025 transformation roadmap in early 2022. For context, this puts us ahead of peers like Procter & Gamble, who reported similar but slightly lower 150 bps expansion last quarter amid their own Superiority Supply Chain push.

Breaking it down by pillar, procurement savings were the standout at $120 million, or 9% below prior-year spend on a like-for-like basis. We achieved this through dynamic hedging on 65% of our cocoa and sugar exposure, which shielded us from the Ivory Coast export restrictions; alternative sourcing for 20% of palm oil volumes from RSPO-certified suppliers in Indonesia, reducing our blended cost by 11%; and AI-powered spend analytics via SAP Ariba, which identified $45 million in supplier consolidation opportunities. In our Beauty & Personal Care category—think products like our flagship GlowEssence shampoos—we negotiated volume commitments with key fragrance houses, mirroring Unilever's playbook, yielding 7% savings on aroma chemicals despite synthetic resin price hikes.

On logistics and distribution, we posted $95 million in savings, driven by a 14% reduction in ocean freight costs and 18% in trucking miles. Regionally, this was huge in North America, where we optimized our DC network post the closure of two legacy facilities in the Midwest, consolidating into three next-gen automated hubs modeled after PepsiCo's direct-to-store delivery efficiencies. We leveraged predictive analytics from Blue Yonder for demand sensing, cutting inventory levels by 22% while maintaining 98.5% on-shelf availability—a critical metric in CPG where out-of-stocks can erode 5-10% of category sales, per Nielsen data. In Europe, facing Red Sea disruptions, we nearshored 15% of beverage concentrate imports from Asia to Mexico, saving 12% on lead times and $18 million in duties. Emerging markets like Brazil and India contributed $25 million via last-mile electrification pilots—our e-truck fleet in São Paulo is now at 40% penetration, slashing diesel costs by 25% and aligning with local ESG mandates.

Manufacturing productivity rounded out the program with $70 million in savings, fueled by a 4.8% lift in Overall Equipment Effectiveness across our 45 global plants. Key technical initiatives included deploying Rockwell Automation's smart factory tech in 12 high-volume lines for snacks—like our CrunchMax chips—boosting throughput by 6% via predictive maintenance that reduced unplanned downtime 30%. We also rolled out GenAI from our partnership with Google Cloud for recipe optimization, reformulating 15% of Household products to lower starch inputs by 8% without compromising taste profiles. In APAC, where labor costs rose 10% due to post-COVID wage pressures, robotic palletizers cut headcount needs by 12% in our Thailand facility.

Strategically, these aren't one-offs; they're baked into our operating model for resilience. We've stress-tested our end-to-end chain against scenarios like a repeat of 2022's Ukraine grain shocks, achieving 95% scenario recovery within 30 days via diversified supplier bases—now 3.2 deep per SKU on average, up from 2.1. Sustainability is embedded too: our Scope 3 emissions dropped 8% YoY from efficient sourcing, putting us on track for SBTi net-zero by 2040, which de-risks us from EU CBAM tariffs. Looking forward, we expect $350 million in FY24 run-rate savings, with 60% flowing to the bottom line after reinvesting 40% into agility projects like blockchain traceability for cocoa, piloted with Mars and Hershey peers, to combat deforestation scrutiny.

This discipline has fortified our 28.5% adjusted gross margin—the highest in five years—and positions us to gain share in a fragmented CPG landscape where peers like Colgate are still playing catch-up on freight resets.
